input.rationale: Section 3.4 lets Customer exit the Agreement or an individual Service Option Attachment on one month's notice at a calendar month end, which beats the 60–90 day fallback ceiling, and IBM has no convenience right: its only Agreement-level termination right is for material breach (3.3), and its only unilateral exit is term-end non-renewal on 90 days' notice (3.2). The fallback fails on one material term — the early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A are open-ended, leaving Customer's exit cost unquantified — so we cap them at three months' charges. We also move "for convenience" so it attaches directly to Customer's termination right (the parenthetical carve-out currently separates them), leaving the qualifier applicable to both the Agreement and any Service Option Attachment. We do not pursue the preferred pro-rata refund of prepaid charges; that gap is noted, not redlined.

proposal.summary: Make Customer's convenience right express and cap early termination charges at three months
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made express that Customer's termination of the Agreement (and of any Service Option Attachment) is for convenience, and capped the Attachment A early termination charges at three (3) months' charges, consistent with our fallback position.
